sanskrit: phalaṃ karmātmakaṃ vidyāt karma jñeyātmakaṃ tathā jñeyaṃ jñānātmakaṃ vidyāj jñānaṃ sadasadātmakam
english: Let one know that fruit has the nature of action, and that action in turn has the nature of the knowable; let one know that the knowable has the nature of knowledge, and that knowledge has the nature of both being and non-being.

sanskrit: jñānānāṃ ca phalānāṃ ca jñeyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ tathā kṣayānte tat phalaṃ divyaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyapratiṣṭhitam
english: When knowledges, fruits, knowables, and actions have all come to their end, that fruit which remains is the divine knowledge, firmly grounded in the knowable.

sanskrit: mahad dhi paramaṃ bhūtaṃ yuktāḥ paśyanti yoginaḥ abudhās taṃ na paśyanti hy ātmasthā guṇabuddhayaḥ
english: That supreme Great Being the disciplined yogins behold; but the unwise do not see it, dwelling within themselves yet bound by an understanding ruled by the qualities.

sanskrit: pṛthivīrūpato rūpam apām iha mahattaram adbhyo mahattaraṃ tejas tejasaḥ pavano mahān
english: Greater than the form of earth is the form of the waters here; greater than the waters is fire, and greater than fire is the wind.

sanskrit: pavanāc ca mahad vyoma tasmāt parataraṃ manaḥ manaso mahatī buddhir buddheḥ kālo mahān smṛtaḥ
english: Greater than the wind is ether, and beyond that is mind; greater than mind is the intellect, and greater than the intellect, it is taught, is Time.

sanskrit: kālāt sa bhagavān viṣṇur yasya sarvam idaṃ jagat nādir na madhyaṃ naivāntas tasya devasya vidyate
english: Greater than Time is the Lord Viṣṇu, to whom belongs all this world; of that God no beginning, no middle, and no end can be known.

sanskrit: anāditvād amadhyatvād anantatvāc ca so 'vyayaḥ atyeti sarvaduḥkhāni duḥkhaṃ hy antavad ucyate
english: Because he is without beginning, without middle, and without end, he is imperishable; he transcends all sorrows, for sorrow is said to be that which has an end.

sanskrit: tad brahma paramaṃ proktaṃ tad dhāma paramaṃ smṛtam tad gatvā kālaviṣayād vimuktā mokṣam āśritāḥ
english: That is declared the supreme Brahman, that is remembered as the supreme abode; reaching it, men are freed from the domain of Time and find their refuge in liberation.

sanskrit: guṇais tv etaiḥ prakāśante nirguṇatvāt tataḥ param nivṛttilakṣaṇo dharmas tathānantyāya kalpate
english: By these qualities things are made manifest; beyond that is the qualityless, which transcends them. The dharma marked by withdrawal likewise leads to the infinite.

sanskrit: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni śarīrāṇi vyapāśritāḥ jihvāgreṣu pravartante yatnasādhyā vināśinaḥ
english: The Ṛc verses, the Yajus formulas, and the Sāman chants, taking refuge in bodies, issue forth upon the tips of tongues—achieved by effort, and perishable.

sanskrit: na caivam iṣyate brahma śarīrāśrayasaṃbhavam na yatnasādhyaṃ tad brahma nādimadhyaṃ na cāntavat
english: But Brahman is not held to be of such a kind, arising from dependence on a body; that Brahman is not to be won by effort, has no beginning nor middle, nor is it subject to an end.

sanskrit: ṛcām ādis tathā sāmnāṃ yajuṣām ādir ucyate antaś cādimatāṃ dṛṣṭo na cādir brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: A beginning of the Ṛc verses, of the Sāmans, and of the Yajus is spoken of; and an end is seen for whatever has a beginning. But no beginning of Brahman is taught.

sanskrit: anāditvād anantatvāt tad anantam athāvyayam avyayatvāc ca nirdvaṃdvaṃ dvaṃdvābhāvāt tataḥ param
english: Because it is without beginning and without end, it is infinite and imperishable; and because it is imperishable it is free of all pairs of opposites, and through the absence of opposites it is the Supreme beyond.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭato 'nupāyāc ca apy abhisaṃdheś ca karmaṇaḥ na tena martyāḥ paśyanti yena gacchanti tat param
english: Because it cannot be seen, because there is no means to it, and because of their deliberate intent upon action, mortals do not behold that by which they might reach the Supreme.

sanskrit: viṣayeṣu ca saṃsargāc chāśvatasya ca darśanāt manasā cānyad ākāṅkṣan paraṃ na pratipadyate
english: Through contact with sense-objects, and through gazing upon the eternal while yet longing in his mind for something else, a man does not attain the Supreme.

sanskrit: guṇān yad iha paśyanti tad icchanty apare janāḥ paraṃ naivābhikāṅkṣanti nirguṇatvād guṇārthinaḥ
english: Whatever men perceive here in the realm of the qualities, that other people desire; they do not long for the Supreme at all, for, being seekers of the qualities, they shun its qualityless nature.

sanskrit: guṇair yas tv avarair yuktaḥ kathaṃ vidyād guṇān imān anumānād dhi gantavyaṃ guṇair avayavaiḥ saha
english: But how shall one who is bound by the lower qualities come to know these very qualities? Only by inference are they to be approached, together with the qualities as their constituent parts.

sanskrit: sūkṣmeṇa manasā vidmo vācā vaktuṃ na śaknumaḥ mano hi manasā grāhyaṃ darśanena ca darśanam
english: By a subtle mind we know it, but by speech we are unable to utter it; for mind is grasped only by mind, and sight only by sight.

sanskrit: jñānena nirmalīkṛtya buddhiṃ buddhyā tathā manaḥ manasā cendriyagrāmam anantaṃ pratipadyate
english: Having purified the intellect by knowledge, and the mind by the intellect, and the host of the senses by the mind, one attains the Infinite.

sanskrit: buddhiprahīṇo manasāsamṛddhas; tathā nirāśīr guṇatām upaiti paraṃ tyajantīha vilobhyamānā; hutāśanaṃ vāyur ivendhanastham
english: He who is bereft of intellect, ill-endowed in mind, and devoid of all desire enters into the state of the qualities; lured astray, such men abandon the Supreme here, as the wind abandons the fire that lies within the fuel.

sanskrit: guṇādāne viprayoge ca teṣāṃ; manaḥ sadā buddhiparāvarābhyām anenaiva vidhinā saṃpravṛtto; guṇādāne brahmaśarīram eti
english: In the taking up of the qualities and in the parting from them, the mind is ever drawn by the higher and lower workings of the intellect; set in motion by this very ordinance, in taking up the qualities it comes to embodiment in Brahman.

sanskrit: avyaktātmā puruṣo 'vyaktakarmā; so 'vyaktatvaṃ gacchati hy antakāle tair evāyaṃ cendriyair vardhamānair; glāyadbhir vā vartate karmarūpaḥ
english: The Person whose self is unmanifest and whose actions are unmanifest passes into the unmanifest at the time of the end; clad in the form of his deeds, he abides among these very senses, whether they wax in strength or wither away.

sanskrit: sarvair ayaṃ cendriyaiḥ saṃprayukto; dehaḥ prāptaḥ pañcabhūtāśrayaḥ syāt nāsāmarthyād gacchati karmaṇeha; hīnas tena parameṇāvyayena
english: Joined with all the senses, this body, once attained, comes to rest upon the five elements; through its incapacity it does not pass on here by action alone, deprived of that supreme imperishable One.

sanskrit: pṛthvyā naraḥ paśyati nāntam asyā; hy antaś cāsyā bhavitā ceti viddhi paraṃ nayantīha vilobhyamānaṃ; yathā plavaṃ vāyur ivārṇavastham
english: A man does not see the end of this earth, yet know that an end of it there shall be; the lures of the world carry the man who is enticed astray, as the wind drives a raft adrift upon the sea.

sanskrit: divākaro guṇam upalabhya nirguṇo; yathā bhaved vyapagataraśmimaṇḍalaḥ tathā hy asau munir iha nirviśeṣavān; sa nirguṇaṃ praviśati brahma cāvyayam
english: As the maker of day, though qualityless, takes on a quality, and may then become an orb stripped of its rays, so too that sage here, having become free of all distinctions, enters the qualityless and imperishable Brahman.

sanskrit: anāgatiṃ sukṛtimatāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ; svayaṃbhuvaṃ prabhavanidhānam avyayam sanātanaṃ yad amṛtam avyayaṃ padaṃ; vicārya taṃ śamam amṛtatvam aśnute
english: The state of no-return, the supreme goal of those rich in good deeds, the self-existent, the imperishable source and resting-place of all that arises—the eternal, deathless, imperishable abode: meditating upon it, one attains peace and immortality.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña puṇḍarīkākṣam acyutam kartāram akṛtaṃ viṣṇuṃ bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O grandsire of vast wisdom, of the lotus-eyed, unfallen Acyuta—Viṣṇu, the maker who is himself unmade, the origin and dissolution of all beings—

sanskrit: nārāyaṇaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ govindam aparājitam tattvena bharataśreṣṭha śrotum icchāmi keśavam
english: of Nārāyaṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, Govinda the unconquered—O best of the Bharatas, I wish to hear of Keśava in his very truth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śruto 'yam artho rāmasya jāmadagnyasya jalpataḥ nāradasya ca devarṣeḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: This matter I have heard as it was spoken by Rāma, son of Jamadagni, and by the divine sage Nārada, and by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana,

sanskrit: asito devalas tāta vālmīkiś ca mahātapāḥ mārkaṇḍeyaś ca govinde kathayaty adbhutaṃ mahat
english: and by Asita Devala, my child, and by Vālmīki of great austerities, and by Mārkaṇḍeya, who tells of Govinda a great and wondrous tale.

sanskrit: keśavo bharataśreṣṭha bhagavān īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ puruṣaḥ sarvam ity eva śrūyate bahudhā vibhuḥ
english: Keśava, O best of the Bharatas, is the Lord, the sovereign, the master; that he is the Person who is all, the all-pervading One, is heard told in many ways.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu yāni vidur loke brāhmaṇāḥ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ māhātmyāni mahābāho śṛṇu tāni yudhiṣṭhira
english: Yet hear now, O mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, those greatnesses of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow which the brāhmaṇas in the world know of.

sanskrit: yāni cāhur manuṣyendra ye purāṇavido janāḥ aśeṣeṇa hi govinde kīrtayiṣyāmi tāny aham
english: And those things which the men learned in the ancient lore declare, O lord of men—all of them concerning Govinda I shall recount in full.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni bhūtātmā mahātmā puruṣottamaḥ vāyur jyotis tathā cāpaḥ khaṃ gāṃ caivānvakalpayat
english: The great-souled Supreme Person, the very Self of beings, fashioned the great elements—wind, fire, and likewise water, ether, and earth.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā pṛthivīṃ caiva sarvabhūteśvaraḥ prabhuḥ apsv eva śayanaṃ cakre mahātmā puruṣottamaḥ
english: And beholding the earth, that lord and sovereign of all beings, the great-souled Supreme Person, made his couch upon the waters.

sanskrit: sarvatejomayas tasmiñ śayānaḥ śayane śubhe so 'grajaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃkarṣaṇam acintayat
english: Composed wholly of radiance, reclining there upon that fair couch, he meditated upon Saṃkarṣaṇa, the firstborn of all beings.

sanskrit: āśrayaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ manaseti viśuśruma sa dhārayati bhūtātmā ubhe bhūtabhaviṣyatī
english: We have heard that the Self of beings holds within his mind the refuge of all creatures, and bears up both that which has been and that which is to come.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin mahābāho prādurbhūte mahātmani bhāskarapratimaṃ divyaṃ nābhyāṃ padmam ajāyata
english: Then, O mighty-armed one, when that great-souled being had manifested, a divine lotus, rivaling the sun, was born from his navel.

sanskrit: sa tatra bhagavān devaḥ puṣkare bhāsayan diśaḥ brahmā samabhavat tāta sarvabhūtapitāmahaḥ
english: There upon that lotus, my child, the divine Lord, illumining the quarters, came into being as Brahmā, the grandsire of all beings.

sanskrit: tasminn api mahābāho prādurbhūte mahātmani tamasaḥ pūrvajo jajñe madhur nāma mahāsuraḥ
english: And when that great-souled one too had been made manifest, O mighty-armed one, there was born of the darkness, before all others, a great demon named Madhu.

sanskrit: tam ugram ugrakarmāṇam ugrāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthitam brahmaṇopacitiṃ kurvañ jaghāna puruṣottamaḥ
english: That fierce one, fierce in his deeds, set upon a fierce intent, the Supreme Person slew, thereby rendering a service to Brahmā.

sanskrit: tasya tāta vadhāt sarve devadānavamānavāḥ madhusūdanam ity āhur vṛṣabhaṃ sarvasātvatām
english: Because of his slaying, my child, all the gods, demons, and men called him Madhusūdana, the bull among all the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: brahmā tu sasṛje putrān mānasān dakṣasaptamān marīcim atryaṅgirasau pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum
english: And Brahmā created sons born of his mind, seven with Dakṣa: Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu.

sanskrit: marīciḥ kaśyapaṃ tāta putraṃ cāsṛjad agrajam mānasaṃ janayām āsa taijasaṃ brahmasattamam
english: Marīci, my child, brought forth Kaśyapa as his eldest son, a mind-born and radiant one, most excellent in sacred knowledge.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhād asṛjad brahmā marīcer api pūrvajam so 'bhavad bharataśreṣṭha dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ
english: From his thumb Brahmā created one even prior to Marīci; he became, O best of the Bharatas, the lord of creatures named Dakṣa.

sanskrit: tasya pūrvam ajāyanta daśa tisraś ca bhārata prajāpater duhitaras tāsāṃ jyeṣṭhābhavad ditiḥ
english: To that lord of creatures, O Bhārata, there were first born thirteen daughters; the eldest among them was Diti.

sanskrit: sarvadharmaviśeṣajñaḥ puṇyakīrtir mahāyaśāḥ mārīcaḥ kaśyapas tāta sarvāsām abhavat patiḥ
english: Kaśyapa, son of Marīci, knower of all the particulars of dharma, of holy renown and great fame, my child, became the husband of them all.

sanskrit: utpādya tu mahābhāgas tāsām avarajā daśa dadau dharmāya dharmajño dakṣa eva prajāpatiḥ
english: Having begotten ten more daughters younger than those, the illustrious Dakṣa, lord of creatures and knower of dharma, gave them to Dharma.

sanskrit: dharmasya vasavaḥ putrā rudrāś cāmitatejasaḥ viśvedevāś ca sādhyāś ca marutvantaś ca bhārata
english: The sons of Dharma are the Vasus and the Rudras of measureless splendor, and the Viśvedevas and the Sādhyas and the Marutvats, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: aparās tu yavīyasyas tābhyo 'nyāḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ somas tāsāṃ mahābhāgaḥ sarvāsām abhavat patiḥ
english: And there were other daughters, twenty-seven younger than these; the illustrious Soma became the husband of them all.

sanskrit: itarās tu vyajāyanta gandharvāṃs turagān dvijān gāś ca kiṃpuruṣān matsyān audbhidāṃś ca vanaspatīn
english: And other daughters brought forth the gandharvas, horses, birds, cattle, the kiṃpuruṣas, fishes, and the sprouting plants and forest trees.

sanskrit: ādityān aditir jajñe devaśreṣṭhān mahābalān teṣāṃ viṣṇur vāmano 'bhūd govindaś cābhavat prabhuḥ
english: Aditi gave birth to the Ādityas, foremost of gods and of great strength; among them Viṣṇu became the Dwarf, and the Lord Govinda came to be.

sanskrit: tasya vikramaṇād eva devānāṃ śrīr vyavardhata dānavāś ca parābhūtā daiteyī cāsurī prajā
english: By that very striding of his the fortune of the gods increased, and the dānavas were overthrown, along with the demonic offspring of Diti.

sanskrit: vipracittipradhānāṃś ca dānavān asṛjad danuḥ ditis tu sarvān asurān mahāsattvān vyajāyata
english: Danu brought forth the dānavas led by Vipracitti, while Diti gave birth to all the asuras, beings of great might.

sanskrit: ahorātraṃ ca kālaṃ ca yathartu madhusūdanaḥ pūrvāhṇaṃ cāparāhṇaṃ ca sarvam evānvakalpayat
english: Day and night, and Time, and the seasons in their turn, the forenoon and the afternoon—all of it Madhusūdana fashioned.

sanskrit: buddyāpaḥ so 'sṛjan meghāṃs tathā sthāvarajaṅgamān pṛthivīṃ so 'sṛjad viśvāṃ sahitāṃ bhūritejasā
english: By his intelligence he created the waters and the clouds, and likewise things moving and unmoving; he created the whole earth, joined together, by his abundant splendor.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇo mahābāhuḥ punar eva yudhiṣṭhira brāhmaṇānāṃ śataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ mukhād asṛjata prabhuḥ
english: Then the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the Lord, brought forth once more from his mouth a hundred excellent brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyaśataṃ vaiśyānām ūrutaḥ śatam padbhyāṃ śūdraśataṃ caiva keśavo bharatarṣabha
english: From his arms a hundred kṣatriyas, from his thighs a hundred vaiśyas, and from his feet a hundred śūdras did Keśava bring forth, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ caturo varṇān samutpādya mahāyaśāḥ adhyakṣaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dhātāram akarot prabhuḥ
english: Having thus brought forth the four classes, that Lord of great fame made the Ordainer the overseer of all beings.

sanskrit: yāvad yāvad abhūc chraddhā dehaṃ dhārayituṃ nṛṇām tāvat tāvad ajīvaṃs te nāsīd yamakṛtaṃ bhayam
english: For just so long as men had the will to sustain their bodies, just so long did they live; and there was no fear wrought by Yama.

sanskrit: na caiṣāṃ maithuno dharmo babhūva bharatarṣabha saṃkalpād eva caiteṣām apatyam udapadyata
english: Nor was there among them the custom of sexual union, O bull of the Bharatas; their offspring came into being by mere will.

sanskrit: tatra tretāyuge kāle saṃkalpāj jāyate prajā na hy abhūn maithuno dharmas teṣām api janādhipa
english: There in the age of the Tretā, offspring were born by will; nor was there among them either the custom of sexual union, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: dvāpare maithuno dharmaḥ prajānām abhavan nṛpa tathā kaliyuge rājan dvaṃdvam āpedire janāḥ
english: In the Dvāpara the custom of sexual union arose among creatures, O king; and so in the Kali age, O monarch, people came under the sway of the pairs of opposites.

sanskrit: eṣa bhūtapatis tāta svadhyakṣaś ca prakīrtitaḥ niradhyakṣāṃs tu kaunteya kīrtayiṣyāmi tān api
english: Thus is proclaimed this lord of beings, his own overseer, my child; but now, O son of Kuntī, I shall recount those peoples who are without an overseer.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāpathajanmānaḥ sarve talavarāndhrakāḥ utsāḥ pulindāḥ śabarāś cūcupā maṇḍapaiḥ saha
english: Born in the southern region are all the Talavaras and Āndhrakas, the Utsas, the Pulindas, the Śabaras, and the Cūcupas, together with the Maṇḍapas.

sanskrit: uttarāpathajanmānaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi tān api yaunakāmbojagāndhārāḥ kirātā barbaraiḥ saha
english: Now I shall recount also those born in the northern region: the Yaunas, the Kāmbojas, the Gāndhāras, and the Kirātas, together with the Barbaras.

sanskrit: ete pāpakṛtas tāta caranti pṛthivīm imām śvakākabalagṛdhrāṇāṃ sadharmāṇo narādhipa
english: These evildoers, my child, roam this earth, sharing the nature of dogs, crows, vultures, and the strong birds of prey, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: naite kṛtayuge tāta caranti pṛthivīm imām tretāprabhṛti vartante te janā bharatarṣabha
english: These did not roam this earth in the Kṛta age, my child; only from the Tretā onward do those peoples exist, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin mahāghore saṃdhyākāle yugāntike rājānaḥ samasajjanta samāsādyetaretaram
english: Then in that most terrible twilight time at the ending of an age, kings clashed together, falling each upon the other.

sanskrit: evam eṣa kuruśreṣṭha prādurbhāvo mahātmanaḥ devadevarṣir ācaṣṭa nāradaḥ sarvalokadṛk
english: Thus, O best of the Kurus, did the divine sage Nārada, beholder of all worlds, declare this manifestation of the great-souled one.

sanskrit: nārado 'py atha kṛṣṇasya paraṃ mene narādhipa śāśvatatvaṃ mahābāho yathāvad bharatarṣabha
english: And Nārada too, O ruler of men, deemed the eternity of Kṛṣṇa supreme, rightly so, O mighty-armed bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ satyavikramaḥ acintyaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣo naiṣa kevalamānuṣaḥ
english: Thus is this mighty-armed Keśava, of true valor, the inconceivable, the lotus-eyed one; he is no mere mortal man.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ke pūrvam āsan patayaḥ prajānāṃ bharatarṣabha ke carṣayo mahābhāgā dikṣu pratyekaśaḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who were the lords of creatures in former times, O bull of the Bharatas? And who are the illustrious sages remembered for each of the several quarters of the sky?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śrūyatāṃ bharataśreṣṭha yan mā tvaṃ paripṛcchasi prajānāṃ patayo ye sma dikṣu pratyekaśaḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O best of the Bharatas, that which you ask of me—who were the lords of creatures remembered for each of the several quarters.

sanskrit: ekaḥ svayaṃbhūr bhagavān ādyo brahmā sanātanaḥ brahmaṇaḥ sapta putrā vai mahātmānaḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ
english: There is one self-existent Lord, the primeval and eternal Brahmā; and of that self-existent Brahmā there are seven great-souled sons.

sanskrit: marīcir atryaṅgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ vasiṣṭhaś ca mahābhāgaḥ sadṛśā vai svayaṃbhuvā
english: Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and the illustrious Vasiṣṭha—they are indeed the equals of the Self-existent One.

sanskrit: sapta brahmāṇa ity eṣa purāṇe niścayo gataḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvān eva prajāpatīn
english: "The seven Brahmās"—such is the settled conclusion arrived at in the ancient lore. Beyond this I shall now declare all the lords of creatures.

sanskrit: atrivaṃśasamutpanno brahmayoniḥ sanātanaḥ prācīnabarhir bhagavāṃs tasmāt prācetaso daśa
english: Sprung from the line of Atri, born of Brahman, eternal, was the Lord Prācīnabarhis; and from him came the ten Prācetasas.

sanskrit: daśānāṃ tanayas tv eko dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ tasya dve nāmanī loke dakṣaḥ ka iti cocyate
english: Of those ten there was a single son, the lord of creatures named Dakṣa; he has two names in the world—he is called Dakṣa, and also Ka.

sanskrit: marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ putras tasya dve nāmanī śrute ariṣṭanemir ity ekaṃ kaśyapety aparaṃ viduḥ
english: Kaśyapa was the son of Marīci; of him two names are heard—one is Ariṣṭanemi, and the other they know as Kaśyapa.
